questions.question: Q: What is projection in dance and why does it matter?

points.text: Projection is the ability to extend energy and presence outward to engage the audience. It matters because it makes the performance compelling and ensures the audience connects with the dance.

questions.question: Q: How can focus be used to show a dancer's relationship with a partner?

points.text: A dancer can direct their gaze at a partner to show connection, look away to show distance, or use shared focus to demonstrate unity in the relationship.

questions.question: Q: Explain the difference between being on the beat and showing musicality.

points.text: Being on the beat means timing movements to the pulse; musicality goes further by responding to accents, dynamics, tempo changes and the emotional character of the music.

questions.question: Q: What is phrasing and how does it improve a performance?

points.text: Phrasing is shaping movement sequences into meaningful units using breath, dynamics and timing. It improves performance by creating contrast, emphasis and clarity, like sentences in speech.

questions.question: Q: Why must physical and technical skills be secure before expressive skills can be effective?

points.text: If a dancer is struggling with technique or physical demands, their attention is on the body rather than communication. Secure technique frees the dancer to focus on expression.
